ITEM NOS. 4 TO 7: 
 
The Board of Aequs Limited recognizes performance-linked, equity-based compensation as an effective 
tool for attracting, motivating, rewarding, and retaining talent across the Company and its subsidiary 
company(ies) and associate company(ies). Such employee ownership programs align employee interests 
with long -term shareholder value creation and foster a culture of ownership and accountability.  
As the Company pursues its growth and expansion objectives, the need to attract and retain key talent, 
particularly in critical and leadership roles, has become increasingly important. Accordingly, the 
Company believes that, in addition to annual incentive  programs, a long -term incentive framework is 
essential to enhance employee engagement, promote a performance -driven culture, and support the 
achievement of the Company's long-term strategic objectives and sustainable growth. 
 
The Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan 2025 (“ ESOP 2025 ” / “ Plan”) was adopted by the Board of 
Directors at its meeting held on May 10, 2025 and members by passing the special resolution at its 
Extraordinary General Meeting held on May 13, 2025 by consolidating all the existing Employee Stock 
Option Plans namely Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan, 2013, Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan, 
2016, Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan, 2020 and Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan, 2022 (“ Prior 
ESOP Plans”) into “Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan 2025” in line with the provisions of the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, as 
amended from time to time, prior to listing of shares of the Co mpany on National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited and BSE Limited on December 10, 2025. The Plan was further ratified by the Board of 
Directors at its meeting held on January 10, 2026, and members by passing a special resolution through 
postal ballot on March 27, 2026, pursuant to which an aggregate pool of 2,04,00,000 (Two Crores Four 
Lakhs Only) equity shares was created for implementation through the Aequs Stock Option Plan Trust  
("Trust"). Out of this pool, the Trust acquired 1,44,00,000 (One Crore Forty-Four Lakhs Only) equity 
shares pertaining to the Company’s earlier employee stock option plans/ schemes and 60,00,000 (Sixty 
Lakhs Only) equity shares under ESOP 2025. As on July 31, 2026, the Trust holds 1,53,38,286 (One Crore 
Fifty-Three Lakh Thirty -Eight Thousand Two Hundred and Eighty -Six) equity shares available for 
utilization under ESOP 2025.  
 
In view of evolving business requirements and talent retention objectives, the Nomination 
Remuneration Committee (“ Committee”) and Board of Directors (“ Board”) at their meetings held on 
August 07, 2026, respectively and subject to your approval, proposed to introduce the ‘Aequs Restricted 
Stock Unit Plan 2026’ ("RSU 2026" or "Scheme" or “Plan”), comprising a pool of 15,00,000 (Fifteen 
Lakhs) Restricted Stock Units ("RSUs").  
 
The proposed RSU pool is intended to be carved out from the existing pool under ESOP 2025, resulting 
in a corresponding reduction of the ESOP 2025 pool to that extent.  
 
The equity shares required for implementation of the proposed Scheme will be sourced from the equity 
shares already acquired, through primary issuance and held by the existing Trust. Accordingly,   
15,00,000 (Fifteen Lakhs) equity shares of face value INR 10/- (Indian Rupees Ten only) each, out of 
the 1,53,38,286 (One Crore Fifty-Three Lakh Thirty-Eight Thousand Two Hundred and Eighty-Six) 
equity shares currently held by the Trust, be earmarked and utilized for implementation of RSU 2026.  
 
=== PAGE 327 of 361 | annual-report/Annual_Report_2026.pdf ===
 
The proposed Scheme would be in the interest of the existing shareholders, as its implementation would 
not result in any additional dilution of equity share capital, given that the Scheme would be administered 
through the utilization of existing shares already acquired and held by the Trust. 
 
This Scheme shall be administered through the existing Trust namely Aequs Stock Option Plan Trust and 
supervised by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.  
 
Performance Evaluation at Grant Stage 
 
In a shift from conventional stock option grant practices, which traditionally after granting RSUs link the 
vesting to achievement of certain performance, the Company is now embracing a more progressive, 
performance-based approach. Under this model, eligib ility for participation in the RSU 2026 will be 
determined at the grant stage basis either corporate or individual performance metrics or both. The 
corporate performance parameters, which will serve as the basis for evaluating the overall success of 
the organization, shall include but are not limited to: 
 
i. Revenue: The revenue generated by the organization either segment wise, consolidated or 
otherwise, with or without its Subsidiary Company(ies) and/or Associate Company(ies) of the 
Company, during the immediately preceding financial year. 
 
ii. Profit After Tax (PAT) : The segment or consolidated net profit after tax realized by the 
organization with or without its Subsidiary Company(ies) and/or Associate Company(ies) of the 
Company, during the immediately preceding financial year. 
 
iii. Additional Commercial Parameters : Any other commercial parameters as determined by the 
Committee either segment wise, department wise or cross functional projects/ assignments, at its 
discretion, based on the prevailing business requirements and objectives from time to time.  
 
To meet the corporate performance criteria, the organization must have achieved or exceeded the 
predetermined thresholds for each of the aforementioned corporate performance parameters as may 
be decided by the committee.  
 
Apart from corporate performance, individual performance shall also be assessed  and each individual 
must achieve a minimum 3 (Three) or meets expectation rating of their designated performance targets, 
as determined through the Company’s established performance appraisal framework.  
 
This performance -based approach ensures a comprehensive and fair evaluation, reflecting overall 
organizational performance and the individual contributions made by employees, thereby supporting a 
transparent, objective, and legally compliant selection and appraisal process. 
 
At the Grant stage, the Committee shall, in its discretion, determine the appropriate quantum of RSUs 
to be granted to the Employees. In making this determination, the Committee may take into account  
both individual and corporate performance, assigning appropriate weight to each, depending on the 
employee's role within the organization. For senior management, a significant weight shall be placed 
on corporate or departmental performance, given their cr itical role in driving the overall performance. 
For middle and junior management, the emphasis shall be more on individual performance, with a 
progressively lower emphasis on corporate performance. This approach is designed to foster the growth 
and success of the organization while simultaneously rewarding employees for their direct contributions 
to creating such value.  However, Committee can exceptionally grant RSUs to key hires with scarce or 
differentiated skills as part of their joining process at the sole discretion of the Committee, considering 
the criticality of the role and skills identified and recommended by management /Committee. 
 
=== PAGE 328 of 361 | annual-report/Annual_Report_2026.pdf ===
 
Save as otherwise provided, by prioritizing corporate performance in the grant process, the Committee 
ensures alignment with shareholder interests, the sustainable growth of the organization, and the 
equitable recognition of employee performance in driving such outcomes. 
 
While granting the RSUs to any eligible employee(s) of any of its subsidiary company(ies) and/or 
associate company(ies), shall at its discretion, consider the factors, including but not limited to the role(s)

a. Description of the Scheme: 
 
Keeping the view of the aforesaid objectives, the eligible employees are expected to receive 
benefits based on their contribution to creating value for shareholders. Such evaluation is made 
at the time of grant. The RSU 2026 contemplates grant of RSUs to t he eligible employees of the 
Company and/ or subsidiary company(ies) and/or associate company(ies) of the Company, 
exclusively working in India or outside India, as determined in terms of the RSU 2026 and in due 
compliance of SBEB Regulations. After vestin g of RSUs, the eligible employees earn a right (but 
not obligation) to exercise the vested RSUs within the exercise period and obtain equity shares of 
the Company subject to payment of exercise price and satisfaction of any tax obligation arising 
thereon.  
 
The Scheme is intended to achieve the following: 
 
(a) to reward and drive performance, and align employees’ individual objectives with the 
Company’s overall growth; 
(b) to align with industry practice, including competitive positioning of overall compensation; 
(c) to provide employees with a wealth creation opportunity. 
 
The Committee shall act as the compensation committee and shall supervise the Scheme. All 
questions of interpretation of the Scheme shall be determined by the Committee, and such 
determination shall be final and binding upon all persons having an interest in the Scheme. 
Whereas the Trust shall administer the Scheme. 
 
b. Total number of RSUs to be granted: 
 
The total number of RSUs to be granted under the Scheme shall not exceed 15,00,000  
(Fifteen Lakhs) RSUs. Each RSU when exercised would be converted into one equity share of face 
value of INR 10/- (Indian Rupees Ten only) each fully paid-up.

and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, as 
amended from time to time , prior to listing of shares of the Company on National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited and BSE Limited on December 10, 2025. The Plan was further ratified by the Board of 
Directors at its meeting held on January 10, 2026, and members by passing a special resolution through 
postal ballot on March 27, 2026.

Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and such other laws, rule s and regulations (including any 
statutory modification(s) or amendment(s) thereto or re -enactment(s) thereof, for the time being in 
force) as may be applicable (“Applicable Laws”). As of July 31, 2026, 1,53,38,286 (One Crore Fifty-Three 
Lakh Thirty-Eight Thousand Two Hundred and Eighty -Six) shares are outstanding with Aequs Stock 
Option Plan Trust, out of a total ESOP pool of 2,04,00,000 shares.  
 
Considering the implementation of Aequs Restricted Stock Unit Plan 2026 (“RSU 2026” or “Scheme” or 
“Plan”) by carving out 15,00,000 (Fifteen Lakhs) stock options from the existing total pool of stock 
options of 2,04,00,000 (Two Crore Four Lakhs) it is nece ssary to amend Aequs Employee Stock Option 
Plan 2025 (ESOP 2025) to reduce its pool from 2,04,00,000 (Two Crore Four Lakhs) to 1,89,00,000 (One 
Crore Eighty-Nine Lakhs).      
 
Further in addition to the above proposed amendment it is also proposed for certain other amendments 
to the ESOP 2025 to, inter alia, to extend the benefits of the Plan to eligible employees of associate 
companies (including joint venture company) in addit ion to, subsidiary compan ies of the Company, 
whether existing or future, in India or outside India, in accordance with the applicable provisions of the 
SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 (the “SEBI SBEB & SE 
Regulations”).  
 
The Board of Directors, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee, at its meeting held on  August 07, 2026, approved, subject to approval of members,  above 
mentioned amendments to the ESOP 2025.  
 
The said amendments to the Plan are not prejudicial to the interests of the employees/ directors of (i) 
the Company; or (ii) Group Company(ies), inter -alia including,  subsidiary companies and associate 
companies [including joint venture company]. 
 
Section 62 of the Companies Act, 2013, the applicable provisions of Companies (Share Capital and 
Debenture) Rules, 2014 read with Regulation 7(1) of the SEBI (SBEB & SE) Regulations, a company may 
vary the terms of employee stock option schemes by way of p assing special resolution by the 
shareholders of such company. Further, in terms of Regulation 6 of SEBI (SBEB & SE) Regulations, the 
approval of the shareholders by way of a separate special resolution is required for granting options to 
the employees of subsidiary companies / group companies (including associate companies, if any) as 
defined in SEBI (SBEB & SE) Regulations / the Companies Act, 2013. 
 
In view of above, approval of the shareholders of the Company is sought by way of special resolutions 
for Item Nos. 9 & 10 of the accompanying Notice. 
 
None of the Directors or Key Managerial Personnel and their immediate relatives are concerned or 
interested, financially or otherwise, except to the extent that the stock options may be granted to any 
of them pursuant to the ESOP 2025.  
 
The Board recommends the Resolutions set forth in Item Nos. 9-10 for the approval of the Members of 
the Company by way of Special Resolutions.

and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

ii. Rationale of the variation of the terms of the “Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan 2025” 
(“ESOP 2025”)  
 
The proposed variation of the ESOP Plan is intended to extend the benefits of the ESOP Plan to 
eligible employees of the associate company (including joint venture companies), whether existing 
or future, in India or outside India, subject to Applicable Law s. The variation seeks to provide a 
broader framework for attracting, retaining, motivating and rewarding eligible employees across 
the group and to align their interests with the long -term growth, performance and value creation 
of the Company and its group companies. 
 
Further, the proposed variation is intended to amend and modify the ESOP pool size of ESOP 2025, 
considering the implementation of Aequs Restricted Stock Unit Plan 2026 (“RSU 2026” or “Scheme” 
or “Plan”) by carving out 15,00,000 (Fifteen Lakhs) stock options from the existing total pool of stock 
options of 2,04,00,000 (Two Crore Four Lakhs) and thereby reducing ESOP 2025 pool from 
2,04,00,000 (Two Crore Four Lakhs) to 1,89,00,000 (One Crore Eighty-Nine Lakhs).  
 
The variation is aimed at providing the Company with greater flexibility in designing and 
administering equity -based incentives, enabling the Company to attract, retain and motivate 
eligible employees through an additional form of long -term equity incentiv e. The proposed 
variation does not adversely affect the interests of the employees who have already been granted 
Options under ESOP 2025, as it pertains only to the ungranted option pool. Consequently, the 
ungranted option pool available under ESOP 2025 sh all stand reduced by 15,00,000 Options, and 
the total pool under ESOP 2025 shall stand at 1,89,00,000 Options, subject to adjustments in 
accordance with the terms of ESOP 2025 and applicable law. 
 
=== PAGE 345 of 361 | annual-report/Annual_Report_2026.pdf ===
 
The proposed variation would also foster a greater sense of ownership and commitment among 
eligible employees and recognise their contribution towards achieving the strategic and business 
objectives of the Company and its group companies. Accordingly, the ESOP Plan is proposed to be 
suitably amended to enable the grant of stock options to such eligible employees, in accordance 
with applicable laws and subject to the terms and conditions of the ESOP Plan.  
 
The proposed amendments also contain certain editorial/drafting changes. The variation in the 
terms of the Plan do not adversely affect any vested rights of the existing option holders.  
 
Further, the proposed changes/deletions/amendments are not detrimental to the interests of the 
employees/ directors of the Company, Subsidiary Company and Associate Company (including joint 
venture companies). 
 
iii. Details of the employees who are beneficiaries of such variation  
 
The beneficiaries of the proposed variation are all existing options grantees (who have not yet 
exercised their options) and such other option grantees to whom options may be granted in the 
future under Plan. 
 
The Plan is to continue to cover the eligible employees of the Company , Subsidiary Company and 
Associate Company in India and abroad, whether present or future.   
 
The Plan will continue to be implemented through Aequs Stock Option Plan Trust (“ Trust”) either 
by primary issue of shares by the Company or secondary acquisition from the open market.  
 
The particulars as required under Section 62 (1)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (SBEB 
&SE) Regulations are provided herein below: 
 
a. Brief Description of the “Aequs Employee Stock Option Plan 2025” (“ESOP 2025”) is as under:  
 
The Company has formulated ESOP 2025 to attract, retain, motivate and reward the deserving 
employees and encourage the employees to contribute to the growth of the Company by granting 
them the option to purchase certain shares of the Company.  
 
The ESOP 2025 shall be administered and implemented by the Nomination & Remuneration 
Committee along with Aequs Stock Option Plan Trust. 
 
b. Total number of employee stock options to be offered and granted:  
 
Considering the implementation of Aequs Restricted Stock Unit Plan 2026 (“RSU 2026” or “Scheme” 
or “Plan”) by carving out 15,00,000 (Fifteen Lakhs) stock options from the existing total pool of stock 
options of 2,04,00,000 (Two Crore Four Lakhs), under ESOP 2025, the maximum number of options 
that may be granted shall be 1,89,00,000 which on exercise would entitle not more than 1,89,00,000 
equity shares of face value of INR 10/- each of the Company, in one or more tranches, on such other 
terms and conditions as the Nomination and Remuneration Committee along with Aequs Stock 
Option Plan Trust, may decide from time to time, subject to any adjustment as may be required. 
 
It is pertinent to note that grant or exercise of any such stock options would not entail any creation, 
issue or offer or new shares in the Company as the corresponding shares are already allotted and 
residing in Stock Option Plan Trust.

ITEM NO. 11  
 
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on April 23, 2026 and May 26, 2026, 
approved the Scheme of Amalgamation between Aequs Limited (“ the Company”/”Transferee 
Company”) and AeroStructures Manufacturing India Private Limited, Aequs Engineered Plastics Private 
Limited and Aequs Force Consumer Products Private Limited (“ Transferor Companies”/”Wholly 
Owned Subsidiaries of the Company ”)  and their respective shareholders and creditors (the 
“Scheme”), pursuant to the provisions of Sections 233 and other applicable provisions of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (the “Act”). 
 
Pursuant to the Scheme and upon the Scheme becoming effective, the respective undertakings, 
businesses, assets, properties, rights, interests, liabilities and obligations of the Transferor Companies 
shall stand transferred to and vested in the Company in accordance with the terms of the Scheme. 
 
Aequs Engineered Plastics Private Limited (“ AEPPL”) is, inter alia, engaged in the business of 
manufacturing of all sorts of plastic products, parts and toys, while Aequs Force Consumer Products 
Private Limited (“AFCPPL”) is, inter alia, engaged in the business of manufacturing all sorts of consumer 
products and toys.  
 
Accordingly, in order to enable the Company to continue, undertake and carry on the businesses and 
activities presently undertaken by AEPPL and AFCPPL, and to align the Object Clause of the 
Memorandum of Association of the Company with the businesses propo sed to be transferred to and 
vested in the Company, it is proposed to alter Clause III(A) of the Memorandum of Association of the 
Company by incorporating therein the relevant main object clauses of AEPPL and AFCPPL.  
 
The business activities presently undertaken by Aerostructures Manufacturing India Private Limited are 
already covered within the scope of the existing Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association of 
the Company. Accordingly, no further alteration of the Memorandum of Association is considered 
necessary in respect of the business and activities of Aerostructures Manufacturing India Private Limited. 
 
The proposed alteration would facilitate the seamless continuation and integration of the aforesaid 
businesses and activities with the existing business operations of the Company and would enable the 
Company to undertake such businesses and activities in a ccordance with its Memorandum of 
Association. 
 
Pursuant to Section 13 of the Act, alteration of the provisions of the Memorandum of Association 
requires the approval of the Members by way of a Special Resolution. Accordingly, the approval of the 
Members is being sought for alteration of Clause III(A) o f the Memorandum of Association of the 
Company in the manner set out in the Special Resolution forming part of this Notice.  
 
The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on  August 07, 2026, has approved the proposed alteration 
of the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association of the Company, subject to the approval of 
the Members and such other approvals, consents, permissions and sanctions as may be necessary.  
 
A copy of the existing Memorandum of Association of the Company, together with the proposed 
alterations thereto, shall be available for inspection by the Members in accordance with the applicable 
provisions of the Act and the details specified in this Noti ce. A draft copy of the revised Memorandum 
of Association with the proposed alterations thereto is also available on website of the Company for 
inspection by the Members up to the last date of remote e-voting.

ITEM NO. 12 
 
In terms of Regulation 23 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ( “SEBI Listing Regulations ”) as amended, any transaction 
with a related party shall be considered material for the Company, if the transaction(s) entered into/ to 
be entered into individually or taken together with the previous transactions during a financial year, 
exceeds 10% of the annual consolidated turnover of the Company (as per Schedule XII of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations) as per the last audited financial statements of the Company, and shall require prior 
approval of Members by means of an Ordinary Resolution. The approval of  the Members under 
Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations is required even if the transactions are in the ordinary 
course of business of the Company and are on an arm’s length basis.  
 
Background and Justification: 
 
Members may take note that Aequs Limited (“Company”) and the below mentioned wholly owned 
subsidiaries of the Company are operating their units from Aequs Special Economic Zone (BAC) and 
Koppal Toy Cluster Koppal (KTC), developed, maintained and operated b y Aequs SEZ Private Limited, 
the Developer of Special Economic Zones within the meaning of SEZ Act 2005 and developer of the 
Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) in KTC. Aequs Limited is operating in BAC since 2008 and subsidiaries are 
operating from BAC and KTC since the inception of their operations.  
 
Aequs SEZ Private Limited being the Developer of BAC and KTC is catering to all the units including the 
third-party units in BAC and also  providing, apart from land and building, all requisite infrastructures 
like electricity, water, transportation and allied services. Aequs SEZ being the Developer of BAC and KTC 
is most equipped to cater all these services, and they have been catering thes e services since 2008 and 
2022 respectively and they are the deemed distribution licensee for supply of electricity. As Aequs and 
wholly owned subsidiaries have chosen to be operating as “Units within the meaning of the SEZ Act 
2005 and rules made thereund er, like most of the SEZ and Industrial parks are operated, Aequs SEZ 
Private Limited being the developer of BAC and KTC are catering all the services to Aequs Limited and 
below mentioned wholly owned subsidiaries and these services are being rendered in t he ordinary 
course of business and at arm’s length price. 
 
The shareholders of the Company had, by way of postal ballot concluded on March 27, 2026, approved 
the material related party transactions proposed to be entered into/continued between the Company 
and its certain wholly owned subsidiaries with Aequs SEZ Private Limited for the financial year 2026-27 
(“In-force RPT Approval”) for an aggregate amount up to INR 1,07,01,44,716/ - (Indian Rupees One 
Hundred Seven Crores One Lakh Forty Four Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixteen only) . 
 
With a view to aligning the validity of shareholders' approval for material related party transactions with 
the Company's annual general meeting cycle and in line with good governance practices, the approval 
of the shareholders is now being sought for the p roposed material related party transactions between 
the Company and its subsidiaries with Aequs SEZ Private Limited for the period commencing from the 
conclusion of the 26 th (Twenty-Sixth) Annual General Meeting until the conclusion of the 27 th (Twenty-
Seventh) Annual General Meeting of the Company, on the terms and conditions set out in the 
accompanying resolution. Though the Company is having In -force RPT Approval in place, as the scale 
and pace of certain operational activities of the Company (including its subsidiaries) are anticipated to 
be accelerated, resulting in an increased requirement for infrastructure and related support services 
being availed from Aequs SEZ Private Limited.
